sentences.text:
Smt Roshni vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November,
2024
 Neutral Citation No. 2024:Mphc-Jbp:55550
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal

On The 11th Of November, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 44647 of 2024
 Smt Roshni
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Ghanshyam Pandey - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri C.M. Tiwari - Government Advocate for the respondent/
 Order

This is the first application filed on behalf of applicant under Section 482 of BNSS for grant of anticipatory bail relating to Crime No. 164/2024 registered by Police Station - Kindari, District Seoni (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 363, 366, 376, 376, 376(2)(N) and 450 of IPC and sections 3, 4, 5 (L), 6 of POCSO Act.
Applicant apprehending her arrest in the aforesaid offence has knocked the portal of this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.
2. As per the prosecution story, allegation against the applicant is that she has given room to the main accused where he has committed rape upon the minor prosecutrix.
On the basis of which, FIR was registered against the applicant under the aforesaid Sections.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
Applicant is a lady.
Prosecutrix has delivered a child and she is living her her parental NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55550 2 MCRC-44647-2024 home.
It is submitted that prosecutrix and her father are present in the Court and they have no objection if the anticipatory bail is granted to the applicant.
Custodial interrogation is not required in the matter.
Therefore, it is prayed to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.

4. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and submitted that present applicant even knowing that prosecutrix is a minor has given room to the main accused where he has committed rape upon the minor prosecutrix.
The mother-in-law and father-in-law of the prosecutrix have denied and stopped the present applicant to give room to the main accused but even then she has provided the room.
Therefore, anticipatory bail may be rejected.

sentences.text: 5. I have heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.

6. Having taken into consideration overall facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the seriousness of offence, I am of the view that it is not a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
7. Consequently, this application under Section 482 of BNSS for grant of anticipatory bail filed on behalf of applicant stands dismissed.
